chunks: Remember when you said to the faithful: 'Is it not sufficient that your Lord should send for your help three thousand angels from the heavens?'
ai.seo_question: What does the verse mean when it asks if three thousand angels are not enough for the believers?
ai.summary: This verse (3:125) serves as the immediate follow-up to the promise of angelic aid, emphasizing that divine support is conditional upon steadfastness (sabr) and prayer (du'a). In Shia exegesis, this highlights the interplay between human effort and divine grace, where the 'three thousand angels' represent the initial surge of spiritual fortitude granted to the believers at Badr.
